Apply online through the School's application system
Submit unofficial transcripts, a personal statement and three letters of recommendation
Submit TOEFL or IELTS scores if from a non-English language university
No GRE requirement and no minimum GPA requirement
The School encourages applicants with backgrounds in any area of biology and non-bioscience backgrounds such as computer science, engineering, math, chemistry and physics

official.application_route: Apply online through the School's application system (Apply Now link on the How to Apply page); all materials due December 1.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible; the School states students come from all over the world, with more than 20 U.S. states and 25 countries represented, and publishes no citizenship or residency restriction.
official.research_requirement: No separate research proposal is required; the ~500-word personal statement must describe the applicant's research interests and include details of research experience.
official.duration: Approximately five years from matriculation to Ph.D.; the average time to degree is 5.19 years
official.description: The School of Biological Sciences at Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory runs an innovative doctoral programme of approximately five years, from matriculation to Ph.D., combining a first year of coursework and laboratory rotations with thesis research under a Research Mentor. The programme matriculates approximately nine students per entering class and is funded largely by an endowment provided by generous private donors. The School pays all tuition costs and associated study fees and provides a stipend of $50,000 per year.
official.region: North America (Cold Spring Harbor, New York)
official.program_type: Ph.D. programme of the CSHL School of Biological Sciences, a division of Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory
official.english_requirement: Students from non-English language universities must submit TOEFL or IELTS test scores; applicants who received their undergraduate and/or master's degree from an institution whose primary language of instruction is English do not have to report a score. The School publishes no minimum TOEFL or IELTS score (TOEFL code 9066, department code 45). IELTS scores are not accepted electronically and must be mailed to the School.

applicant_utility.summary: Funding is automatic on admission rather than a separate scholarship: the School pays all tuition and associated study fees and provides a $50,000 annual stipend, which rises to $55,000 or your fellowship amount if you win an external NSF/NIH-type award. There is a single annual cycle that opens each September and closes hard on December 1, with every document including recommendation letters due by then, an August start, and covered interviews late January to mid-February. You apply to the School, not to a lab: individual professors cannot offer admission, so do not spend the autumn cold-contacting PIs before applying.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Final-year undergraduates or master's students with genuine lab research experience in any bioscience, or with backgrounds in physics, maths, computer science, engineering or chemistry, who want a small (about nine per class), fully funded doctorate with no GRE and no GPA cut-off.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your three referees by mid-November: letters are uploaded by referees through the Embark system, none arrive after December 1, and the School advises allowing at least one month for letter writing.
Merge scanned unofficial transcripts from every institution you have attended into a single PDF before uploading; official transcripts are not needed.

Draft the ~500-word personal statement around the three published prompts (motivation for a biological sciences career, research interests, fit with CSHL) and fold in research experience, employment and any publications.
If your degree was not taught in English, register early for TOEFL (code 9066, department 45); note that IELTS only exists on paper and must be mailed to Urey Cottage.
Budget the $75 application fee and self-report any GRE/TOEFL/IELTS scores in the Academic History section, since admissions cannot confirm receipt of test scores.
Proofread everything before submitting: once submitted, an application cannot be revised, added to or corrected.
common_rejection_risks: A referee who never completes the upload: the three letters arrive through referee-triggered emails from the Embark system, and a missing letter on December 1 ends the application.
Assuming a rolling deadline or a second round: there is only one admission cycle per year and no materials of any kind are accepted after December 1.
Incomplete transcript set: forgetting to merge transcripts from every attended institution into one document can leave the file incomplete at review.
Editing after submission: the School does not allow adjustments, additions or revisions, so an error or missing document stays as filed.
Relying on a PI's informal interest: an individual professor cannot admit a student, so no lab 'offer' substitutes for admission through the School.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: US student-visa fees and personal spending beyond the stipend; tuition, fees, insurance, relocation, laptop, the lab research allowance and interview travel are all covered by the School.
document_audit: Unofficial transcripts are accepted, but every institution attended must be represented and merged into one file.
IELTS is not accepted electronically: paper scores must be mailed to Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory, Urey Cottage, One Bungtown Road, Cold Spring Harbor, NY 11724, so allow postal lead time.
Referees must upload letters themselves; faxed, mailed or emailed recommendation letters are not accepted.
Referee emails come from the Embark application system and can land in spam, so warn your referees to look for it.
alerts: December 1 is absolute: the School accepts no materials after the application closes, including recommendation letters.
Applications open only in the Fall term for an August start; other start dates are not possible.
The School also now advertises a separate BioAI Ph.D. track for AI and computational-biology applicants, so check which programme fits before applying.
No minimum TOEFL/IELTS score is published, but scores are mandatory for degrees not taught in English, so book tests early in the autumn.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the online form, upload merged transcripts and the personal statement, register three referees for upload and pay the $75 fee, with everything in by December 1; shortlisted candidates are notified by email by the end of January and interview from late January to mid-February with travel, accommodation and meals covered.
